resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded StartYear1=2017, StartYear2=2021 - both years are directly and independently confirmed (Phase 1 in service 2017; final phase fully in service January 2021). POSSIBLE GAP TO FLAG: Enbridge's own 10-K separately states 'the second phase of the Atlantic Bridge project ... placed into service in the ... fourth quarter of 2019' (discussed in the same filing, in year-over-year revenue commentary), i.e. there appear to have been THREE distinct in-service milestones (2017, 2019, 2021) under Enbridge's own phase numbering (Phase III = the one completed Jan 2021), but the sheet's Start fields only carry two years (StartYear1=2017, StartYear2=2021) with StartYear3 blank. Recommend the orchestrator check whether a 2019 in-service date belongs in StartYear3/StartYear3Month - it is not fabricated here since it isn't the unit's recorded value, but it is a documented milestone the sheet does not currently carry.

verifications.note: 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab, row 871 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1': 'Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)' = 40 - an exact match to the recorded Capacity=40.00 MMcf/d.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Capacity=40.00 MMcf/d. EIA's federal pipeline-projects tracker gives exactly 40 MMcf/d as the additional capacity of Phase 1 of this project (completed 2017), an exact match. Tier set to medium rather than high because only one source states this specific 40 MMcf/d figure. FLAG FOR VALIDITY: both Enbridge's 2020 10-K ('Atlantic Bridge Phase III ... to transport 133 million cubic feet per day (mmcf/d)') and a contemporaneous Utility Dive report ('will add 132,700 dekatherms/day to the region's capacity') independently state the TOTAL capacity of the full, multi-phase Atlantic Bridge project as ~133 MMcf/d, not 40 - the recorded 40.00 MMcf/d appears to capture only the 2017 Phase 1 increment (per EIA's own phase-by-phase breakdown: Phase 1 = 40 MMcf/d, Phase 2 (US) = 93 MMcf/d, cumulative ~133), not the project's full built-out capacity. Not changing the value (that is a validity call, not this leg's job), but flagging the apparent undercount for the orchestrator/validity leg.

verifications.note: 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab, row 871/1014: Beg_State = 'NJ' for both Atlantic Bridge phases, matching recorded StartState/Province=New Jersey exactly. Row 1015 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase 2 (CAN)' (Maritimes & Northeast leg): State(s) = 'MA, NH, ME, NB', i.e. Maine is an explicit through-state on the route before it crosses into New Brunswick, Canada.

'Atlantic Bridge is a 132,700 Dth/d expansion of the Algonquin and Maritimes & Northeast pipeline systems in New England, designed to flow south-to-north into Canada.' Confirms the New Jersey-to-New-England corridor and its ultimate direction into Canada.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded StartState/Province=New Jersey, EndState/Province=Maine (both US). Start point (NJ) is confirmed exactly by EIA (Beg_State=NJ on both phases). FLAG FOR VALIDITY, not treated as a contradiction: EIA's own project rows list the US-jurisdiction Algonquin phases as ending in Massachusetts (End_State=MA), with Maine appearing only as a pass-through state on the separate Maritimes & Northeast (Phase 2 CAN) leg, whose own End_State is New Brunswick, Canada - i.e. the pipeline system this project expands continues past Maine into Atlantic Canada (also stated in the NaturalGasIntel piece: 'designed to flow south-to-north into Canada'). Recording EndState/Province=Maine/EndCountryOrArea=United States is consistent with Maine being the last US state on the route (and GGIT may track the Canadian continuation as a separate entity), but it is not the pipeline's literal physical terminus per these sources - flagging so the orchestrator can confirm GGIT's convention here matches intent rather than an oversight.

verifications.note: Headline: 'FERC Allows Conflicted Contractor to Supervise Enbridge's Atlantic Bridge Gas Project.' Body: 'In early 2015, when FERC first hired ERM to review the then-proposed Atlantic Bridge, Spectra Energy was promoting the project. Yet last year, Canada's Enbridge purchased Spectra.' Names the project and states Enbridge's ownership directly, dated after the Feb. 2017 Enbridge-Spectra merger.

'The $452 million project by Algonquin, an affiliate of Calgary-based Enbridge Inc., has been built in phases...' Independently, from a different publisher, names the project and its Enbridge affiliation.

Enbridge Inc.'s own 2020 Form 10-K discusses 'Atlantic Bridge Phase III' and the earlier phases as 'our' commercially secured growth projects, without any joint-venture partner named (unlike, e.g., the same filing's EMF and T-South entries, which explicitly disclose partial/JV interests) - consistent with wholly-owned status.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Owner1=Enbridge/100%. Three independent sources (DeSmog, NaturalGasIntel, and Enbridge's own SEC 10-K) confirm Enbridge as owner/sponsor of the project (via its Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC subsidiary), with no source naming any co-owner. None of the three states the '100%' figure as a bare number; the 100% attribution rests on the absence of any disclosed partner across all three sources plus the 10-K's own pattern of flagging partial/JV interests elsewhere in the same document when they exist (e.g. EMF, T-South) but not for Atlantic Bridge. Not contradicted by anything found.
